name: pipe_pressure_drop_correlations
title: Pressure drop in straight pipes: friction factors and two-phase correlations (function library)
summary: EES FUNCTION library of the pipe pressure-drop correlations: six single-phase Darcy friction factors (Churchill 1977, Swamee-Jain 1976, Konakov, Petukhov 1970, Haaland 1983 and Cheng for supercritical CO2), the single-phase pressure drop of a straight pipe (Darcy-Weisbach plus hydrostatic term), the two-phase frictional pressure drops of Friedel 1979, Muller-Steinhagen & Heck 1986 and Choi-Kedzierski-Domanski 2001, the two-phase acceleration term (homogeneous or Zivi void fraction) and the two-phase gravity term; the Reynolds, Froude and Weber numbers, the homogeneous and Zivi void fractions and the homogeneous two-phase density are given as helper functions.

authors: P. K. Swamee and A. K. Jain (Swamee-Jain friction factor, 1976)
L. Cheng (Cheng supercritical CO2 friction factor, 2024)
Z. Yang and J. Yang (pseudo-critical temperature of CO2, 2012)
H. Muller-Steinhagen and K. Heck (two-phase pressure drop, 1986)
J. Y. Choi, M. A. Kedzierski and P. A. Domanski (Choi two-phase pressure drop, 2001)
G. B. Wallis (two-phase acceleration pressure drop, 1969)
origin.license: MIT (declared in pyproject.toml; LICENSE.txt of the library is Apache-2.0) / model published under the library MIT licence
origin.notes: LaboThapPy commit f03f7f47, file labothappy/correlations/pressure_drop/pipe_DP.py, with the helpers of labothappy/correlations/properties/dimensionless.py (compute_reynolds, compute_froude, compute_weber), labothappy/correlations/void_fraction/void_fraction.py (void_fraction_homogeneous, void_fraction_zivi), labothappy/correlations/properties/two_phase.py (compute_two_phase_density) and labothappy/correlations/properties/supercritical.py (pseudo_boiling_bounds, pseudo_critical_temperature_CO2). The demonstration cases come from the library example labothappy/component/examples/heat_exchanger/hex_pipe_DP_correlations_comparison_example.py. Translation published under the CoolSolve_Library MIT license (decision D3); the scientific basis of each correlation is the original paper named in its function comment block.

verification.reference: the LaboThapPy correlations of commit f03f7f47, recomputed in a throw-away virtual environment under work/ (work/pipe_dp/ref_pipe_dp.py, installed with pip install -e ~/git/LaboThapPy); the five friction factors also reproduce the values printed by the library example itself at the Reynolds number of its logspace grid; 34 output values in total
verification.notes: compare_solution.py: 34 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); the largest relative deviation is 1.0e-12 (dP_F3, supercritical CO2), i.e. round-off in the double-precision evaluation.
